newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO officials say Hebron deal with Israel close.
newsitem.headline: PLO officials say Hebron deal with Israel close.

text.p: Palestinian officials said on Thursday that Israel and the PLO had resolved the main issues holding up the long-delayed Hebron redeployment and an agreement could be announced within 24 hours.
"There might be some problems in the drafting but the issues have been resolved," said one of the officials, who declined to be identified.

"If there are no problems in the drafting, within 24 hours there will be positive results and an agreement. The only remaining issue is the drafting of the protocol which explains the steps of implementing the Hebron redeployment," he said.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators were meeting in Eilat in Israel and Taba in Egypt, neighbouring Red Sea resorts, to hammer out an agreement on the long-delayed pullback from the West Bank town.

Israel has held up a redeployment, citing security concerns for the 400 Jews who live and study in enclaves among 100,000 Arabs. The city is sacred to Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.

Israeli spokesman Moshe Fogel declined comment, except to say: "Talks on both sides, Eilat and Taba, are continuing. We are at the point where both sides are trying to identify points of mutual understanding."
